# Datum

> Datum replaces legacy CDNs, DIY networks, and fragmented infrastructure with a network cloud built for agents: connected infrastructure for AI companies, backed by open source. A Kubernetes-style API, no feature gates. Available as public cloud, as Dedicated Cloud for scaled deployments, or as open source (AGPLv3). Free until billing begins February 1st, 2027, then usage-based with no seat fees; a credit card is required at signup.

Agents act through `datumctl` (a CLI built on the Kubernetes apiserver, also runnable as a local API proxy and an MCP server) or directly against the HTTP API at `https://api.datum.net`. The API is self-describing: `datumctl api-resources` lists every resource type and `datumctl explain <resource>` returns its schema, so an agent can learn the full surface at runtime.

## Act
- [Agent home](https://agents.datum.net): canonical, machine-readable entry point for agents.
- [llms-full.txt](https://www.datum.net/llms-full.txt): full technical reference — concepts, IAM, resource kinds, getting started.
- [Docs MCP](https://www.datum.net/docs/mcp): hosted MCP server to search and read Datum docs.
- [datumctl docs](https://www.datum.net/docs/datumctl): install, auth, commands, plugins.
- API base `https://api.datum.net`: Kubernetes-style paths, e.g. `/apis/resourcemanager.miloapis.com/v1alpha1/organizations`.
- Local authenticated gateway: `datumctl api proxy` serves the API on `127.0.0.1` with your session attached and auto-refreshed — no token handling.
- MCP: the `datumctl ai` toolset runs as an MCP server; an official self-hosted Datum MCP server integrates with Cursor.

## Core verbs (datumctl)
- `datumctl api-resources` — list every resource type.
- `datumctl explain <resource>[.<field.path>]` — schema and field docs (e.g. `datumctl explain httpproxies.spec`).
- `datumctl get | describe | diff | apply | delete` — read and manage resources. `apply` has conflict management and is safe to retry.
- `datumctl auth login --no-browser` — device-code login for SSH sessions, VMs, and containers.

## Pricing
Usage-based, no seat fees. Datum Cloud is free until billing begins February 1st, 2027; a credit card is required at signup to head off fraud and abuse, and you are notified before billing starts. Full rates: https://www.datum.net/pricing

- Galactic VPC egress to the public internet: first 200 GB free, then $0.05/GB (to 10 TB), $0.04/GB (10–150 TB), $0.03/GB (150–500 TB); 500 TB+ contact sales. Ingress and same-region internal transfer are free; cross-region is $0.03/GB.
- DNS $0.60/M requests after the first 500K; ALB $1.00/M requests; GSLB (soon) $0.60/M requests.
- Compute $0.0504/vCPU-hour and $0.0162/GiB-memory-hour; Tunnels $0.01/endpoint-hour; Object Storage (soon) $0.0085/GB-month standard, $0.024/GB-month performance.
- Always free: datumctl, permissions and team invites, Secrets, Metrics Export, Audit & Activity Logs, SSO, Service Accounts, Datum MCP, AI Assistant (Patch), Domains, Desktop Apps.

For a demo, [reach out](https://www.datum.net/contact/).

## Use cases
- Hyperscale-style networking, private-by-default agentic workloads, edge workloads, and GPU/CPU capacity (Dedicated Cloud) for inference clouds, sandboxes, and frontier labs. See https://www.datum.net/use-cases

- [Public changelog](https://www.datum.net/changelog/): meaningful platform improvements.
- Next: Galactic VPC, Connectors, GSLB, Edge Apps, Object Storage, Interconnects (AWS/GCP).
